correctness.rationale: With equal normalized angular-mass boundary components, e_n=z^n/sqrt(1+q^n) for 0<q<1; S=M_z is a bilateral weighted shift with weights squared w_n^2=(1+q^(n+1))/(1+q^n). The diagonal self-commutator is w_n^2-w_(n-1)^2=(1-q)^2 q^(n-1)/[(1+q^(n-1))(1+q^n)], and reflections n=-k and n=k+1 give each delta_k twice. Strict ratio <1, telescoping gives Tr D=1-q and trace class. h=-log q, g_q(k)->g(x)=1/(4cosh^2(x/2)), exponential geometric bounds justify Riemann sums for every fixed p>0 and t>=0, giving B(p,p) and I(t)=integral log(1+t g(x)) dx=arcosh^2(1+t/2). At threshold a in (0,1/4), double-counted points with g(x)>a yield 4 arcosh(1/(2sqrt a)); differentiating the upper-tail function gives density 2/[y sqrt(1-4y)]. Spectral convergence is vague away from zero, not weak finite-mass convergence. Independent rational Laurent-basis differences and sample continuum convergence checked; infinite limits derived analytically.
